text: No, the 2025 tree-cover loss was not due to land clearing for agriculture. The loss area (13.5 ha) overlapped with 13.1 ha of native forest, with no planted forest involved. While Hansen GFC detected the loss in 2025, no follow-up observations in later years were available to confirm agricultural conversion. The high JRC forest agreement (98%) in 2020 supports the area being forested before the loss, but without post-2025 data, we cannot determine the cause. The event met the 30% tree-cover threshold but lacked corroboration from later years, making it likely natural (e.g., fire, disease) rather than deliberate clearing for farming.
